contentHtml:
With over five decades of expertise in construction and infrastructure, Renaatus Group has taken another step forward with the 𝐬𝐨𝐟𝐭 𝐥𝐚𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐡 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐄𝐍𝐀𝐅𝐋𝐄𝐗 𝐅𝐢𝐛𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐨𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐚𝐭 𝐍𝐀𝐓𝐂𝐎𝐍 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔, organised by the Association of Consulting Civil Engineers (ACCE), Coimbatore.

Powered by 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝐋𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐫 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡𝐧𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐲 and Renaatus’ expertise in real world building requirements, RENAFLEX is designed to meet the changing demands of contemporary construction.

The outcome is a 𝐡𝐢𝐠𝐡 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐅𝐢𝐛𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐨𝐚𝐫𝐝 that delivers:

• High Impact Strength
• Fire Resistance
• Water Resistance
• Superior Flexural Strength
• Dimensional Stability
• Sustainable Performance

For architects, engineers, builders and contractors, RENAFLEX offers a dependable solution for stronger, safer and longer-lasting structures.

Manufactured at 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐬’ 𝐚𝐝𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐚𝐭 𝐍𝐚𝐢𝐝𝐮𝐩𝐞𝐭𝐚, 𝐀𝐧𝐝𝐡𝐫𝐚 𝐏𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐡, 𝐑𝐄𝐍𝐀𝐅𝐋𝐄𝐗 marks a 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐧𝐞 in the company’s journey towards 𝐢𝐧𝐧𝐨𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 and 𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞.

The event was attended by dignitaries from the engineering fraternity like 𝐇𝐨𝐧’𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢. 𝐑𝐚𝐣𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐫𝐚 𝐑𝐚𝐨 𝐊𝐚𝐥𝐛𝐚𝐯𝐢, 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐀𝐂𝐂𝐄, 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢. 𝐂. 𝐉. 𝐑𝐚𝐠𝐡𝐮𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧, 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧, 𝐍𝐀𝐓𝐂𝐎𝐍, 𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐑. 𝐒𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐡 𝐊𝐮𝐦𝐚𝐫 (𝐑𝐞𝐭𝐝.), 𝐀𝐂𝐂𝐄 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 and the 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 𝐭𝐞𝐚𝐦 𝐨𝐟 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐬 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐩 under the guidance of 𝐌𝐫. 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐯𝐚 𝐒𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐦, 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧 & 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐨𝐫.

𝐑𝐄𝐍𝐀𝐅𝐋𝐄𝐗 is a step towards innovation and engineering excellence; manufactured at 𝐑𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐚𝐭𝐮𝐬’ 𝐚𝐝𝐯𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐚𝐭 𝐍𝐚𝐢𝐝𝐮𝐩𝐞𝐭𝐚, 𝐀𝐧𝐝𝐡𝐫𝐚 𝐏𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐡.

🌍 From Legacy to Innovation
🚀 Plant 4 – Bhoomi Pooja Ceremony | Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh

Every milestone begins with a vision, and every legacy is strengthened through innovation.

Today marks a defining moment in Renacon’s growth journey as we proudly performed the Bhoomi Pooja for Plant 4 (RF4) – our upcoming high-capacity manufacturing facility for AAC Blocks and Rapid Wall Panels at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh.

This auspicious occasion was graced by our esteemed leadership:

✨ CMD: Mr. R.P. Selvasundaram
✨ Executive Director: Mrs. Padmini Sundaram
✨ Managing Director: Mr. Manoj Poosappan
✨ President: Mr. Manikavasagam

This plant is set to become Renacon’s largest manufacturing facility, with an impressive production capacity of:

🏭 2,000 m³ of AAC Blocks per day and 60000m3 per month.

🏗️ 30,000 Rapid Wall Panels per month

this expansion significantly enhances our ability to serve the growing demand for modern construction solutions and further strengthens our position to become the leading building materials brand in South India.

With four manufacturing facilities, Renacon is building a strong foundation to lead the region through:

✅ Advanced manufacturing technology
✅ Sustainable and eco-friendly solutions
✅ Superior product quality and operational excellence
✅ Faster delivery and enhanced customer service
✅ A commitment to supporting India’s rapidly growing infrastructure needs

Plant 4 is more than a new factory—it is a symbol of our ambition, our innovation, and our unwavering belief in building a smarter and more sustainable future.

As we lay the foundation stone today, we are not just constructing another manufacturing facility; we are shaping the future of construction in India.

✨ 𝐎𝐮𝐫 𝐇𝐨𝐧’𝐛𝐥𝐞 𝐂𝐡𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐧 – 𝐌𝐫. 𝐑. 𝐏. 𝐒𝐞𝐥𝐯𝐚 𝐒𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐦

Renacon Rapid Wall Panels are built to last and are highly resistant to wear and tear. This durability makes them suitable for reuse in other projects after initial installation. Whether panels are removed during renovations or moved to new locations, they retain their structural integrity, minimizing the need to produce new materials for each project.

    Easy Dismantling and Reinstallation

    One of the standout benefits of Renacon Rapid Wall Panels is their ease of installation and removal.
    Their lightweight design allows for easy transportation and reinstallation with minimal damage. This feature makes them ideal for temporary structures, renovations, or relocations where materials need to be reused efficiently.

    Reduction of Construction Waste

    Construction waste is a significant environmental challenge, with large amounts often ending up in landfills. By reusing Renacon Rapid Wall Panels, construction companies can cut down on waste output considerably. This reusability supports eco-friendly building practices and aligns with the industry’s focus on reducing waste.

    Versatility in Reuse

    Renacon Rapid Wall Panels are versatile and can be reused in various types of construction, whether residential, commercial, or industrial. Their adaptability means they remain valuable assets even after their initial use, making them easy to repurpose for different structural needs in future projects.


    Conclusion

    The reusability of Renacon Rapid Wall Panels offers a robust solution for sustainable construction. By extending their life cycle through reuse, builders can reduce waste, save costs, and support greener building practices. As the industry embraces circular economy principles, Renacon Rapid Wall Panels provide a forward-thinking, eco-friendly choice that supports the future of construction.

Autoclaved Aerated Concrete Blocks – A revolution in the Construction Sphere

Ever since the Autoclaved Aerated Concrete blocks came into existence, the construction sphere has witnessed a great turnaround. This lightweight concrete component has a longstanding history that makes it a highly reliable and a perfect alternative to the conventional red bricks and its associated components.

So, What when did AAC first step-in?

The traces of the Autoclaved Aerated Concrete was first witnessed in the mid-year of 1920. Proofs of history also reveal that this was at first invented in Sweden which then owing to its supremacy witnessed a massive outreach amongst the other European countries. From thereafter, the evolution of AAC blocks turned the tables in the international market. Industries started flooding in numbers to figure out what AAC blocks are all about. There were, in fact, numerous recce’s on the origin and usability of the AAC blocks that aided in a better understanding of the lightweight building material. Since it’s launch step into the Indian market in early 2000, the construction sectors had their eyes popped out at this highly durable building material.

Autoclaved Aerated Concrete – The AAC blocks is a blend of several supplementary components that include Cement, fly ash, sand, aluminum powder, limestone, and gypsum.

The basic inclusions of Fly Ash, Gypsum, Lime, and OPC are initially fed as a whole into the pouring mixture alongside aluminum powder that’s added as a separate component. These upon further processing undergo Block casting on mould; and then leads to demoulding and wire cutting. The wire-cut blocks are then placed under high-pressure Steam Curing for nearly 12 hours and the result – lightweight & durable AAC Blocks.

The AAC blocks are superior in quality that they can be utilized for both interior and exterior construction purposes. Ever since the arrival of AAC Blocks in the Indian Market, there’s a greater buzz for these products owing to its reliability and durable properties. This has, in fact, led to a transition shift in the construction arena. Both Builders and Customers have started to have a sneak peek on the AAC Blocks and its advantages. A lot of industrial studies and researches are been continually set up to have a briefer and better insight on the implementation of AAC Blocks and its associated products.

But then, the factual proofs and dimensional studies have largely provided a greater stand on the implementation of AAC blocks. Moreover, it is evident from the reports that the Autoclaved Aerated Concrete is the Next Big Thing in the Construction Sphere.

Coming Closer to You with Highest Manufacturing Capacity, Competitive Pricing and Faster Delivery.

Blockmaker eyes savings on logistics

Renaatus Procon, part of the RPP Group, is investing ₹50 crore to set up a plant at Tirunelveli to produce AAC (Autoclaved Aerated Concrete) blocks.

Chairman and managing director of the group, R.P. Selvasundaram, and CEO of Renaatus Procon G. Suresh Kumar told the media that RPP started a plant near Chennai in 2011 to make AAC blocks consisting of fly ash and cement.

These blocks are used largely in high-rise buildings and infrastructure projects.

The Tirunelveli plant will be operational by 2019. The firm’s main markets for its Renacon brand are Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. The total capacity of the two plants is 3 lakh cubic meters a year. As a logistics account for 25-30% of the product cost, Renaatus plans to have regional plants. “By 2022, we want to set up a plant in another State,” Mr. Kumar said.

The country has about 100 plants making AAC blocks and the market is growing 15% annually.

Chemicals tie-up

Another focus area for Renaatus is construction chemicals. It draws inputs for the business from a German firm and is now exploring a technical tie-up.

The group’s interests span construction projects, M-Sand, ready-mix concrete, and AAC blocks. Its annual turnover is ₹350 crore and its target is ₹600 crore by 2020.
